text:
oliver: Ran an nsys + perfetto double-run on the new batch policy (adaptive-burst) — seeing a sharp KV cache miss spike around t=120ms into long-seq requests. nvprof shows a kernel switch to the generic matmul_fallback for a subset of launches.

marta: can you paste the nsys qdrep? any command used? :eyes:

oliver: sure, saved qdrep at s3://redwood-debug/nsys/1798453012-qdrep.qdrep. nsys cmd:

``
nsys profile -o out --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cudnn --force-overwrite --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- ./run_inference --batch-policy=adaptive-burst
``

kevin: interesting — fallback kernel would explain perf regression. did kernel selector change after the quantization patch? recent commit 6f3a2 changed kernel priority order.

priya: quick note: prefix (KV) reuse rate dropped from ~78% to ~52% for this workload? heatmap attached in perf dashboard. Could be batching reordering evicting cache entries.

oliver: exactly, when adaptive-burst groups by size we see higher sequence length skew which increases prefix fragmentation. Perfetto timeline shows repeated cache eviction events aligned with cudaMalloc/free churn.

marta: can you attach a small timeline snippet? a 10s perfetto slice would help. Also please capture per-request IDs with TRACE_POINT to map eviction events to request ids.

oliver: uploaded a perfetto trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/2ff3ab (slice 00:10 - 00:20). Kernel timeline: lots of small memcpy kernels interleaved, then a big generic_gemm launch.

perf-bot: deploy 1798f7 -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark:

kevin: hypothesis: our kernel selector falls back when workspace allocation can't be satisfied for fused kernels. adaptive-burst increases concurrent mem pressure causing fragmentation. We should try preallocating large workspace pools per device and test.

priya: also try forcing batching by sequence length (group by seqlen) to preserve prefix locality. if reuse improves, cache hit rate should climb and the regression disappears.

oliver: reproducer plan: 1) baseline run with old selector + prealloc; 2) new selector without prealloc; 3) new selector with grouping-by-seqlen. I'll attach nsys qdrep for each.

marta: for the nsys analysis, run `nsys stats` to get kernel counters and do `nvprof --analysis-metrics` if needed. Also capture `nvtxRangePush` around cache ops.

oliver: got it. starting runs now. ETA ~45m.

kevin: neat. once you have qdrep, run the kernel classification script and post the CSV (kernel_name, avg_ms, launches, selector_path) so we can triage.

oliver: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
